heroHeadline: FCC Adopts 7x Satellite Capacity Rules; $42.45B BEAD Rural Broadband Goes Operational
heroSubtitle: The FCC voted April 30 to replace decades-old satellite spectrum limits with performance-based rules enabling a sevenfold gain in LEO broadband capacity — a direct boon for Starlink and Amazon Leo reaching underserved regions. The same day, the $42.45 billion BEAD program became operational across US states, targeting the final 7 million unserved locations. Starlink has now crossed 10 million direct subscribers globally, with 10,020+ satellites in orbit and a target of 25 million subscribers by end-2026.
footerNote: Data sourced from ITU, GSMA, World Bank, A4AI, SpaceX regulatory filings, Amazon, FCC, and major international research outlets. Contested figures noted with confidence levels.
